newsitem.title: USA: Developer plans 1.4 million-square-foot Boston complex.
newsitem.headline: Developer plans 1.4 million-square-foot Boston complex.

text.p: New York City-based Millennium Partners, which has run into expansion problems at home, unveiled plans Tuesday for a 1.4 million-square-foot complex on a piece of choice Boston real estate.

The privately financed $250 million project will be anchored by a 4,700-seat Sony multiplex theatre and Reebok Sports Club, mirroring the real estate developer's Lincoln Square project on New York's Upper West Side, the developer said in a statement.
But a spokesman for the Boston Redevelopment Authority said the city has not been formally informed of the size of the project and the developers have not yet filed those plans.
"If there are any tax breaks or incentives, I'm not aware of them," BRA spokesman Guy Bourgault said.

Boston Mayor Thomas Menino, who has been trying to revitalise the city's downtown for years, heralded the news, saying the project known as Millennium Place "will bring life and energy (to the downtown). Millennium Partners has a great track record of revitalising areas and turning them into thriving urban destinations."

But Millennium Partners plans for expansion in New York City have hit a snag. They agreed to pay more than $300 million to the Metropolitan Transportation Authority upon signing a contract for the New York Coliseum just a few blocks from their Lincoln Square development. But New York Mayor Rudolph Giuliani is objecting to the deal, which is for a 64-story glass tower and connecting complex.

The developers' agreement calls for them to pay the money, lawsuits or no lawsuits -- and lawsuits are expected. The height of an earlier proposed building on the site that borders Central Park contributed to that deal falling through.

Millennium Partners secured $300 million in June from Goldman, Sachs & Co.'s Whitehall Fund, financier George Soros and his Quantum Realty Fund and a group of German investors to back a fund to finance five or six projects totalling about $1.25 billion in various U.S. cities, the developers said.

Millennium Partners, in conjunction with WDG Ventures, is in the process of building a four-story, $180 million retail complex operated by Sony in San Francisco. Coincidentally, it was one of 30 corporations which do business with that city or need city permits to donate $10,000 or more to help underwrite last month's U.S. Conference of Mayors.

Millennium Partners has also paid more than $200,000 for air rights over part of the Massachusetts Turnpike in an area bordering Boston's Back Bay neighbourhood. The plan also calls for a huge entertainment complex, residential towers, retail shops and a hotel.
